Season One: Alive and A New Beginning
Like every living being, "Xel" first breath wasn’t perfect.

Shortly after the initial release of Season One: Alive, a technical issue was discovered:
The magical clock, meant to be alive and dynamic, was malfunctioning, stuck at a static time.

To preserve the integrity of the project and honor the experience of collectors, the release was paused, and the previous tokens were carefully burned.

Now, the revived and corrected version has returned, refined, reliable, and alive, ensuring that every mint offers a unique and authentic experience.

31762.d:
Seven appetites. One endless mouth.

GLUTTONY — The Maw is a generative ritual about insatiable hunger and digital decay. Each token is born from on-chain entropy and rendered in p5.js: a living vortex that swells, contracts, and slowly devours a cloud of drifting pixels. Every mint reveals one of seven hunger states —from Crimson Hunger to Abyssal Maw—each with its own palette, particle behaviour, and pulse cadence.

This project sits at the crossroads of mythology, psychiatry, and glitch aesthetics. Desire becomes geometry; compulsion becomes motion; pixels bleed. Collectors are not just owners but witnesses to a system that can never be full. Feed it with your gaze—then watch it starve and swell again.
31762.c: The edition you hold embodies one of the seven hunger states. Its palette, particle swarm, and maximum stretch radius are unique to your fxhash seed and will never repeat. Screen-capture or record at any moment—the Maw will look different each time it breathes.

31782.d:
The first chapter of the Seven Digital Sins cycle explores our contemporary relationship with consumption in the digital age. GLUTTONY transcends physical appetite — it manifests as our endless scroll, our insatiable hunger for more content, more stimulation, more digital fulfillment that never truly satisfies.

"Crimson Hunger" visualizes this state of perpetual craving through abstract digital forms that pulse and breathe with an organic hunger. The piece captures the psychological tension between desire and void, creating an unsettling beauty that mirrors our collective digital compulsions.

This inaugural release serves as both artistic statement and technical exploration — a minimal viable product that tests the boundaries between generative art and psychological commentary.
31782.c:
"Crimson Hunger" is a singular digital artifact that visualizes our contemporary relationship with endless consumption. This unique piece presents an abstract manifestation of digital appetite — organic forms that pulse and breathe with an unsettling hunger against a void-like background.

The work captures the psychological tension of our digital age: the constant craving for more content, more stimulation, more digital fulfillment that never truly satisfies. Created as an experimental statement piece, it serves both as standalone art and as the foundation for potential future explorations in the Seven Digital Sins cycle.

31783.d:
Bauhaus Solstice: Where Nature Meets Minimalist Obsession

I’ve been chasing two loves for as long as I can remember: the solstice, that fleeting moment when the Earth leans into its extremes of light and shadow, and the Bauhaus movement, with its pursuit of form stripped to its essence. Bauhaus Solstice is where these collide, and I've loved pouring them into this artwork.  

The solstice makes me reflect twice a year on so many things, the world pauses at its brightest or darkest, from London’s endless summer days to Patagonia's’ winter hush. It connects us all through these universal shifts, no matter where we stand. Then there’s Bauhaus: those clean lines, that fearless minimalism, the way every shape and stroke has its place.

Bauhaus Solstice splits the canvas in half, a nod to the solstice’s Yin and Yang, light on one side, dark on the other, flipping randomly like the universe tossing a coin. Semicircles, inspired by Bauhaus’s geometric purity, cross the divide. I pulled data for cities worldwide. Stockholm’s 18-hour days, Darwin’s balmy solstice nights. A random one takes centre stage each time, its details (date, sunrise, longest day) laid out in the Bauhaus93 font.
  
I built it as an SVG for that crisp, infinite scalability, Embedding the Bauhaus93 font as Base64 so the artwork stays true wherever it goes.

Press ‘s’ to save as an SVG or ‘p’ for a PNG.  

It’s for anyone who’s ever stared at the sky or lost hours dreaming in clean lines and bold contrasts.

31793.d:
A living codex of Leonardo da Vinci's lost studies, born from algorithmic imagination

  Each piece in this collection presents an authentic Renaissance manuscript page, as if discovered from Leonardo's personal notebooks.
  Through generative algorithms, we recreate the master's eye for detail, his obsession with natural forms, and his pioneering spirit of
  scientific inquiry.

  The Collection

  Every artwork is a unique manuscript page featuring one or more of four study types:

  - Flying Machine Studies - Mechanical wings and aviation apparatus with authentic engineering precision
  - Bird Studies - Anatomical investigations of avian flight with skeletal accuracy
  - Geometric Forms - Sacred geometry explorations using golden ratio proportions
  - Mechanical Devices - Intricate gear systems and Renaissance engineering

  Historical Authenticity

  What makes this collection extraordinary is its commitment to period authenticity. Each manuscript exhibits:

  - Renaissance Paper - Handmade textures with authentic aging, foxing, and watermarks
  - Historical Inks - Period-accurate pigments (sepia, iron gall, bistre, red chalk) with realistic fading patterns
  - Mirror Writing - Leonardo's characteristic reversed Italian annotations and calculations
  - Quill Pen Texture - Natural pressure variations and ink flow irregularities
  - Renaissance Measurements - Historical Florentine units and proportional systems

  The Manuscript Experience

  Many pieces feature multiple studies per page, echoing Leonardo's actual working methods where he would fill every inch of precious paper
  with investigations. The layouts respect authentic Renaissance page proportions while incorporating his signature technical annotations,
  mathematical calculations, and engineering construction marks.

  Collecting History

  This isn't just generative art - it's a portal to the Renaissance mind. Each piece represents a moment of discovery, a scientific
  breakthrough, or an artistic revelation that might have emerged from Leonardo's workshop. The randomized parameters ensure that no two
  manuscripts are alike, yet each maintains the authentic voice of the master.

31798.d:
CENTURY-XXX-METALOEWENSBERG is an homage to Ohne Titel (1969–1970) by Verena Loewensberg.

2 of 5 in CENTURY-XXX, Series 2
Edition of 128

CENTURY-XXX is a series of software sketches that pay tribute to artists of the 20th century. Each piece is named after a specific artist and reimagines one of their original works through code, often by adding motion, variation, or interactive elements. These sketches don’t replicate the original artworks but instead extend their core ideas into new forms.

By “software sketch,” I mean something more informal than a finished artwork. While some of my projects take months or even years to complete, these sketches are created quickly—often in just a few days. They may be lighter in process, but they’re equally important to me. Sketching with code is how I think through ideas and discover new directions for future work.

The project began with the CENTURY exhibition at DAM Projects in Berlin in fall 2012, where I premiered Network C, Network D, and the first Signal to Noise software piece. Since then, these sketches have inspired more full-scale artworks like METASOTO, METAVASARELY, METAMOLNAR (also known as Hommage à Molnar), including the eponymous CENTURY released through Art Blocks in June 2021.

CENTURY-XXX Series 1 was released from December 2021 to January 2022 in editions of 1,000. The first artwork in Series 2 followed in October 2022, also in an edition of 1,000. The remaining four works in Series 2 are scheduled for release starting in 2025, each in smaller editions of fewer than 128 based on what feels appropriate for the individual piece.

The long-term vision for CENTURY-XXX is to create 100 software sketches, each one inspired by a different artist and artwork from the 20th century.

31799.d:
this animated artwork explores the concept of obsession, where thoughts endlessly loop and repeat, spiraling into themselves with relentless intensity.
a sequence begins, persists, and returns to itself, like a cycle that can't be broken.
it represents the mind fixating on a singular idea, where every iteration builds upon the last, yet never reaches resolution.

the work embodies the compulsion to revisit, rework, and refine — to return to the same thought or action repeatedly, despite the absence of closure.
it reflects the ceaseless pull of obsession, where focus narrows to a single point, and every detail becomes magnified.
the energy of obsession is both captivating and exhausting, driving the work forward while tethering it in place.

as the artwork unfolds, it reveals the hypnotic nature of entrapment, drawing the viewer into a labyrinth of endless variations.

the final form is intricate, dense, and complex, a structure that seems to go nowhere and everywhere at once.
this work does not aim to resolve the obsession—it immerses the viewer in the endless loop, allowing them to feel the pull of obsession, the tension of its constant reappearance, and the overwhelming power it holds.

31804.d:
Scale is a generative art project that explores the hypnotic beauty of animated geometric patterns through concentric rectangles and flowing color gradients. Each iteration creates a unique visual symphony where mathematical precision meets organic movement.

The artwork features multiple rectangular grids, each containing concentric layers that pulse and rotate with animated color streams. These color bands flow continuously across each rectangle's surface, creating an infinite loop of chromatic motion that never repeats exactly the same way twice.
